messages.author: 784daa35bfa5ee27
messages.subject: msn analysis with filtered mlgs
parts:
Hi Zhian,

Can you please help me with the following?

I have contacted 260 MLGs into 249 contracted MLLs using mlg filter function. (after choosing the appropriate cutoff threshold using cuttoff predictor). I used bruvo's distance and Farthest neighbor algorithm.

I want to incorporate the contracted mlgs in the msn analysis, but want to use the Nei's distance, as I've noticed Bruvo's does not produce nice plots.

However, when I use the the following commands I do not get the proper mlg ids on the nodes.

field_dist <- nei.dist(field, warning = TRUE)
min_span_net <- poppr.msn(field, field_dist, showplot = FALSE, include.ties = TRUE, mlg.compute = "contracted",  threshold=0.05681818, clustering.algorithm = "farthest_neighbor")

set.seed(69)
plot_poppr_msn(field,
               min_span_net,
               mlg = TRUE,
               gadj = 4,
               nodescale = 13,
               palette = c('#a6cee3','#1f78b4','#b2df8a','#33a02c','#fb9a99','#e31a1c','#fdbf6f','#ff7f00','#cab2d6','#6a3d9a'),
               cutoff = NULL,
               quantiles = FALSE,
               beforecut = TRUE,
               pop.leg = TRUE,
               size.leg = FALSE,
               scale.leg = TRUE,
               layfun = igraph::layout_nicely) 

My question is does the filtered information during the msn analysis and if not how do you call it within poppr.msn?

Thanks in advance!
P.S.- Poppr is an amazing tool :)
Ruvini

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] msn analysis with filtered mlgs
parts:
Hi Ruvini,

I'm afraid that you cannot filter your data with one distance and create the MSN with another.

My suggestion would be to stick with Bruvo's distance and play around with different igraph layouts OR find the cutoff for Nei's distance that gives you the same number of MLGs with the `filter_stats()` function (fuller examples will be provided in the upcoming version of poppr).

The problem with using two different distances is the fact that they will group MLGs into different lineages based on their own assumptions. An example would be two samples that differ by one mutational step across all loci. They would collapse beyond a threshold of 0.5 for Bruvo's distance, but represent infinite Nei's distance.
